observation: On an unmodified repository, immediately after 'init install-assets --agent=claude' and with no edit to any projected file, 'init doctor' reports '[WARN] Managed assets [claude skills]: current=2, stale=16' and '[WARN] Managed assets [claude subagents]: stale=3', while 'init status' on the same state reports '[OK] claude skills: no stale managed entries', '[OK] claude subagents: no stale managed entries' and then lists all 18 skills and all 3 subagents as current.

evidence.summary: init doctor: [WARN] Managed assets [claude skills]: current=2, stale=16 / [WARN] Managed assets [claude subagents]: stale=3. init status, same repository state: [OK] claude skills: no stale managed entries / [OK] claude subagents: no stale managed entries, followed by all 18 skills and 3 subagents listed as current.

hypothesis: doctor and status compute staleness against different sources - most likely doctor resolves the canonical asset root from the configured skills-root (docs/agents/skills, which is empty in a host repository that only consumes package-owned assets) while status compares against the manifest and the installed files.
validated_conclusion: Two commands must not disagree about whether managed assets are current. Whichever is right, the WARN teaches a host to re-run a sync that changes nothing, and after that the host has no way to tell a real drift from this noise.
